items.title: Holman Bill — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: We had just done I’m Gonna Go Fishin’ for Peggy Lee. That was lyrics she’d written to a Duke tune. So I recommended that to Gerry, to make a jazz chart on that.

ctx.x: I was going to now switch to Carmen McRae and the L.A. Philharmonic. Again, I‟m trying to capture the breadth and the versatility that is a hallmark of your career.

The orchestra – I hadn‟t written much for strings: a little bit for Peggy and a little bit on some pop records that I‟d done sweetening dates for. So it was a little bit scary in that way, but I imagined a well mixed thing. As it turns out, when they have the soloist with the orchestra, and she‟s got a rhythm section, that‟s all you‟re going to hear, is the rhythm section and the singer. The orchestra is way in the back. So that was the first disappointment, because I had envisioned this big carpet of sound…
